task_instance: Run the wow-digest for today: pull the last 24h of newsletter emails and Telegram channel posts, filter noise, score the survivors for genuine surprise against the user's focus/research context, and append 3-7 WOW items under '## Reading' in today's daily note (Daily/YYYYMMDD.md).
blocker_detail: The skill's entire workflow is to execute its bundled Python scripts (scripts/ingest.py, enrich.py, salience_filter.py, wow_score.py, feedback.py), which the office-assistant runtime cannot do: it grants only reading/writing/editing text files and web fetch/search, and explicitly cannot run code, scripts or shell commands. The scripts are present next to SKILL.md, so they are not missing; they simply cannot be run here. Beyond code execution, the pipeline also depends on capabilities the runtime does not have and the safety rules forbid: ingest.py shells out to a workspace mail CLI to list/fetch the user's Gmail newsletters and to a separate Telegram client script (in a telegram-telethon skill that is not part of this skill's repo) to pull channel posts (both require an authenticated account/connector), and wow_score.py reads a personal vault and invokes an LLM to score items. None of the ingestion sources or the scoring model can be reached without running code and connecting to account-bound services, so no real candidates can be gathered and no verifiable digest can be produced.
evidence: Read SKILL.md: workflow step 1-7 is 'Run scripts/ingest.py ... wow_score.py ...' then append to daily note and archive emails via a mail CLI. Glob of the skill repo shows scripts/{ingest,enrich,salience_filter,wow_score,feedback}.py and config/{sources.yaml,wow_prompt.txt} are all present. Read scripts/ingest.py: ingest_email() calls subprocess.run([mail-CLI, 'gmail', 'users', 'messages', 'list'/'get', ...]) and ingest_telegram() calls subprocess.run([python, ~/.claude/skills/telegram-telethon/scripts/tg.py, 'recent', ...]) - both require executing code and an authenticated Gmail/Telegram account. Read scripts/wow_score.py head: reads a personal '~/Brains/brain' vault and imports subprocess/os to call an LLM for scoring. Attempting the core deliverable requires running these scripts; the runtime forbids running any code, so the deliverable cannot be produced or verified. No replacement/stub was written per the run rules. No files outside the work directory were modified; only result.json was written in the work directory.
